- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.5) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and slow downward slope.  
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.3) and model is forecasting a strong upward trend, reduce forecast slope to avoid overconfidence bias.  
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.3) and model is forecasting a flat or downward trend, reverse the bias — shift forecast upward by 2–5% to reflect sentiment momentum.  
- Model tends to underpredict true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile — add 1–3% buffer to early forecast points.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.2), model often fails to capture momentum — smooth forecast curve to avoid abrupt swings.
